prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / companion playing-card illustration. Image 1 is the APPROVED FINISHED Design 2 King of Spades and is the authoritative reference. Create ONE matching King of DIAMONDS by changing only that King's identity, conventional pose and suit-specific colors. Match the approved card's exact 5:7 composition, reduced head-and-torso scale, broad sleeves spanning the interior near the center, rich yellow Ming silk round-collar dragon robe, red inner collar, jeweled plaque belt, black yishanguan cap with folded upward wings, dense Chinese lotus floral fields on BLACK ground, shaped antique-white reserve with fine gold tracery, diagonal woven waist join and small turquoise center jewel. Preserve the same fine warm outlines and softly shaded naturalistic Chinese faces/hands. Keep the luxurious yellow, teal, madder, ivory and gold balance. Do not enlarge the figure or reduce the floral density. The cap is Ming headwear, not a European crown or Qing conical hat. Preserve the narrow gold lotus-vine outer band, beaded gold rules, margin, and diagonal ivory corner panels at their exact source positions.
Exactly two opposing waist-up depictions of the same man. The lower portrait, hands, weapon, robe, background and index must be the precise 180-degree rotated counterpart of the upper, elegantly joined at the exact canvas center. Same face, age, costume and pose in both halves. Keep ALL caps, weapon tips, hands and accessories within the inner frame, with visible clearance. No objects may cross the border.
Single flat full-canvas card asset about 1060x1484, no mockup, scenery, watermark, extra lettering, new medallions, extra heads or limbs. Only the two K letters and two small solid suit symbols in the index panels. Graceful correct hands and clearly readable weapon grips.
DIAMONDS-SPECIFIC CHANGES: Image 2 supplies ONLY the Madder Lake border color, not an empty layout. Change the outer border ground to Madder Lake #A73443 while preserving the gold lotus vines. Keep the DENSE INTERIOR floral ground BLACK. Change both indices to red serif K and small plain red DIAMOND rhombi; retain index panel positions and rotated orientation.
Give this King a distinct mature Chinese face with a strong nose, neatly groomed black moustache and a short tapered beard. STRICT 90-DEGREE SIDE PROFILE FACING VIEWER'S LEFT. Exactly ONE EYE visible; no second eye or far eyebrow, no three-quarter angle. Clear nose silhouette and back of the head on the right. This strict profile is the essential conventional identity of the King of Diamonds. Lower portrait must have the identical one-eyed profile rotated 180 degrees. Same Ming yishanguan cap and yellow dragon robe family; small differences in dragon embroidery allowed.
WEAPON: completely replace the jian sword with a recognizable ONE-HANDED SINGLE-HEADED CHINESE-INSPIRED AXE, upright on viewer's RIGHT beside/behind the shoulder. Dark straight wooden shaft with restrained gilt bronze fittings; compact steel crescent axe blade mounted crosswise at the top, its cutting edge facing inward toward the king. Clear axe geometry: one lateral crescent blade with a short opposite poll, no spear point or sword blade, no giant fantasy axe, no halberd, no bronze-age dagger-axe. Blade entirely within the inner frame, top around y=16% of canvas, no crossing border or cap. One anatomically natural visible hand grips the shaft at chest height. His other hand is hidden inside a draped sleeve, not an extra inherited Spades sword hand. Preserve the reduced torso scale and broad robe span. Lower half repeats the same axe and hand under 180 degrees.
